impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO contributes to the Apply AI Strategy by delivering validated AI agent systems across the strategy's priority application sectors. The clinical decision support demonstrator (WP5, D5-02) establishes an evidence-based pathway for AI agent adoption in healthcare, directly advancing Apply AI's healthcare priority through integration with HL7 FHIR clinical data sources and specialist sub-agent coordination (IMP-2, linked to OUT-4). The manufacturing demonstrator (WP6, D6-02) achieves measurable efficiency and quality improvements — targeting ≥15% defect reduction and ≥10% energy savings in an operational pilot factory — advancing Apply AI's advanced manufacturing priority (IMP-3, linked to OUT-5). The logistics transfer demonstrator (WP7, D7-02) confirms cross-sector portability of the MAESTRO architecture, extending Apply AI Strategy adoption potential to additional European economic sectors and providing transferability evidence for further scaling (IMP-4, linked to OUT-6). All three demonstrators are validated against sector-specific benchmarks and are designed for post-project scaling through EDIH and industry partner channels.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO directly advances European open strategic autonomy by creating a complete, European-origin AI agent technology stack that does not depend on proprietary non-European platforms. The neuro-symbolic planning engine (WP2, D2-02), adaptive tri-store memory architecture (WP3, D3-02), and formally verified coordination protocols (WP4, D4-01, D4-02) constitute a differentiated European paradigm for trustworthy AI agents, established through IMP-1 (Advancement of European AI agent technology to global leadership position). The integrated MAESTRO framework (WP8, D8-02) and open-source community platform (WP9, D9-02) make this stack freely available to European researchers and companies under IMP-5 (Strengthening the European AI innovation ecosystem), directly reducing European dependency on proprietary non-European AI agent platforms. The standardisation pathway (IMP-6: ≥1 proposal submitted to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE, traceable to D4-01) positions European-developed coordination protocols as the basis for international AI agent standards, reinforcing European regulatory and technical leadership consistent with the Destination framing of the call.

The open-source MAESTRO framework (WP9, D9-02) and benchmark suite specification (WP8, D8-01) are shared as communicable results on the AI-on-demand platform under IMP-5, with targets of ≥5 external research groups formally adopting the benchmark and ≥10 European SMEs/startups building on the MAESTRO framework. The integrated framework release (WP8, D8-02) packages all research pillar components (planning D2-02, memory D3-02, coordination D4-02) as a communicable, deployable artifact accessible to the wider European research community. Scientific publications from WP2–WP4 prototype development target ≥20 peer-reviewed papers in NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAMAS, and AAAI, with ≥100 citations within 3 years of publication (IMP-1 indicators), representing a substantial contribution to the global AI research record with a European-origin identity.

The AI-on-demand platform contribution route (D9-02) creates the primary access pathway through which AI Factories, Data Labs, and TEFs can retrieve, deploy, and validate MAESTRO components. An explicit AI Factory, Data Lab, or TEF partnership or named validation activity is not documented in Tier 3. This gap should be resolved by project partners before Phase 8 drafting.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO delivers real-world AI agent impact across two of the three priority sectors with full TRL 5 demonstrators, and provides architectural transferability evidence for the third. The healthcare demonstrator (WP5, D5-02) validates AI-assisted clinical diagnostic reasoning on 500 de-identified cases with specialist sub-agent coordination, targeting acceptance of the clinical validation report by ≥1 national health technology assessment body (IMP-2 indicators). The advanced manufacturing demonstrator (WP6, D6-02) validates multi-agent real-time coordination in an operational pilot factory, targeting ≥15% defect reduction and ≥10% energy savings (IMP-3 indicators). For in-vehicle autonomous driving, IMP-4 includes an explicit indicator: 'Architectural transferability mapping to in-vehicle autonomous driving completed', with D7-02 (Logistics demonstrator system prototype) as the deliverable from which this analysis is produced. MAESTRO does not deliver a dedicated in-vehicle autonomous driving deployment demonstrator; the in-vehicle sector impact is addressed through architectural transferability mapping rather than a full operational deployment. This partial coverage is consistent with MAESTRO's positioning as one project in the call's portfolio approach to multi-sector coverage, and with EI-06's own Inferred status in Tier 2B.

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All MAESTRO peer-reviewed publications are made open access in compliance with Horizon Europe open access mandates, deposited in open repositories (arXiv and institutional repositories) at the point of acceptance, with no embargo. Software outputs — including the planning engine (D2-02), adaptive memory architecture (D3-02), coordination protocol implementation (D4-02), integrated MAESTRO framework (D8-02), and open-source community platform (D9-02) — are released under the Apache 2.0 permissive licence via GitHub and the AI-on-demand platform. The benchmark suite (D8-01, D8-03) and evaluation datasets are published in FAIR-compliant, machine-readable formats with documented metadata schemas. A Data Management Plan (DMP) deliverable is produced within the first 6 months of grant signature and updated periodically as required by the RIA instrument and Horizon Europe open science requirements.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: MAESTRO adopts an open-source-first IPR strategy consistent with its strategic objective of reducing European dependency on proprietary non-European AI agent platforms (IMP-5). Core software outputs — planning engine (D2-02), adaptive tri-store memory architecture (D3-02), coordination protocol implementation (D4-02), integrated MAESTRO framework (D8-02), benchmark suite (D8-01, D8-03), and open-source community platform (D9-02) — are released under the Apache 2.0 permissive licence to maximise European SME and research community reuse and commercial adoption without licence barriers. The multi-agent coordination protocol specification (D4-01) is submitted for international standardisation through ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE in preference to patent protection, to maximise interoperability and embed European technical leadership in global AI standards. Sector-specific application outputs from the healthcare (WP5), manufacturing (WP6), and logistics (WP7) demonstrators may be subject to partner-specific IPR measures governed by the consortium agreement, including potential patents or trade secrets for sector-specific adaptations, provided such measures do not restrict access to the core MAESTRO framework. All EU-funded results remain accessible to the Union in accordance with Horizon Europe grant conditions and the applicable Model Grant Agreement.

sustainability_mechanism.description: MAESTRO results are sustained post-project through four complementary mechanisms that do not depend on continued project funding. First, the open-source MAESTRO framework (WP8, D8-02; WP9, D9-02) is established as a community-governed project with a formal contribution governance model adopted by M36, targeting ≥10 European SMEs/startups and ≥5 external research groups as active adopters by M48 — creating a self-sustaining open-source development and user community that continues framework maintenance and extension beyond the project lifetime. Second, the AI-on-demand platform listing (M36 per KPI-04-B and KPI-05-A) ensures permanent discoverability and institutional access to MAESTRO framework components and benchmark evaluation protocols through durable European digital infrastructure, supporting long-term use by AI Factories, Data Labs, and Testing and Experimentation Facilities (TEFs) without dependency on consortium maintenance. Third, sector-specific institutional adoption creates self-sustaining deployment pathways: ≥3 hospital networks with post-project adoption instruments for the MAESTRO clinical decision support demonstrator (IMP-2, KPI-01-A, D5-03) and ≥5 manufacturing SMEs engaged in technology transfer through EDIH partners (IMP-3, KPI-01-B, D6-03) establish institutional continuity in two of the three call priority sectors, with adoption processes initiated within the project lifetime and structured to continue under hospital and SME own resources. Fourth, the standardisation submission for MAESTRO formally verified multi-agent coordination protocols (IMP-6, D4-01) embeds core MAESTRO technical contributions in international AI standards through ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE, providing regulatory-level persistence and ensuring that MAESTRO's coordination paradigm continues to influence the European and global AI agent technology landscape independently of any single consortium partner's continued investment.
